learningObjective: Separate the training objective (continued pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, or preference optimization) from the parameter-update scope (full weights or a parameter-efficient adapter such as LoRA).
mediumRationale: A two-panel semantic comparison is the smallest useful spatial explanation: the first panel orders objectives by the signal they learn from, while the second makes parameter-update scope a separate choice that applies after selecting an objective.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because a single flowchart would falsely make LoRA a terminal stage after SFT or preference optimization; the learning task is to separate two axes, not follow one branching process.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected because the distinction is categorical rather than geometric or quantitative, and fixed SVG labels would wrap less naturally at a 390 CSS-pixel viewport.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected because two labelled panels expose the orthogonal choices in ordinary reading order, use established responsive primitives, and preserve all meaning as selectable text in dark mode and print.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because toggling objectives or update scopes would hide valid combinations and add controls without improving the stable two-axis mental model.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the reviewed papers contain method-specific architecture and training figures, but none teaches this objective-versus-update-scope distinction. Reuse permission is either limited or unnecessary, so no source figure, layout, wording, result, or data is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the prose presents four items as peer modes even though LoRA and QLoRA can implement parameter-efficient updates for a selected training objective; readers need a spatial separation to avoid treating objective and update scope as one axis.

pages.insight: The preceding slide covers tokenization and perplexity, establishing the language-model objective context but no adaptation choice.

The text-representation slide distinguishes feature-based transfer from fine-tuning pretrained parameters on downstream tasks, but predates modern parameter-efficient adapters and preference optimization.
The following slide covers recurrent architectures and memory networks and adds no fine-tuning taxonomy.
The preceding transformer overview explains model architecture and training objectives but does not separate post-training objective from update scope.

The strongest relevant slide contrasts instruction tuning, in-context learning, and RLHF, and explicitly says instruction tuning is supervised while RLHF changes response tendencies; it does not cover LoRA or DPO.
The following LLM slide distinguishes base, instruction-trained, and RLHF models and discusses tool use, but adds no adapter-based training mechanism.
A system-design checklist briefly suggests fine-tuning one base model per user group for personalization; it supplies an operational use case but no objective or parameter-update comparison.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of the local PDF were text-indexed page by page for fine-tuning, instruction tuning, in-context learning, few-shot learning, pretraining, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, RLHF, and preference optimization. The directly relevant transfer-learning neighborhood on pages 98-100 and LLM adaptation neighborhood on pages 103-105 were rendered and visually inspected in full. Page 165 was also reviewed because it mentions per-group fine-tuning. The deck contains no LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, or two-axis objective-versus-update-scope treatment. No deck artwork, screenshots, wording, examples, or layout is reused.
deckReview.license: The local deck states no reuse license and includes third-party figures with mixed or incomplete attribution. It is treated as review-only material; the implementation is original semantic HTML.

sources.title: Don't Stop Pretraining: Adapt Language Models to Domains and Tasks
sources.usage: Used as the primary source for domain-adaptive continued pretraining on unlabeled domain text before task-specific fine-tuning.
sources.license: The paper is used only as a technical reference. No figure, table, result, wording, or visual structure is reproduced.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
sources.usage: Used as the primary source establishing LoRA as frozen pretrained weights plus trainable low-rank matrices, which makes it an update-scope mechanism rather than a distinct data objective.
sources.license: The arXiv record uses the arXiv perpetual non-exclusive distribution license, which limits third-party reuse. No paper figure, equation, benchmark result, wording, or layout is reproduced.

sources.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
sources.usage: Used as the primary source for backpropagating through a frozen quantized base model into LoRA adapters, supporting the separation of storage and update strategy from the chosen fine-tuning objective.
sources.license: The source is used for technical verification only. No paper figure, equation, memory result, wording, or layout is reproduced.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
sources.usage: Used as the primary source for direct optimization on preference pairs relative to a reference policy without fitting a separate reward model or running PPO.
sources.license: The source is used for technical verification only. No paper figure, equation, empirical result, wording, or layout is reproduced.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that the article mixes two independent decisions. Continued pretraining, SFT, and preference optimization specify the training signal and intended behavioral change. Full fine-tuning versus PEFT specifies which parameters are trainable and how adaptations are stored or served. An original two-panel visual makes the non-peer relationship explicit without asserting a universal quality or cost ordering.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages, rendered and inspected both relevant slide neighborhoods, and checked primary sources for continued pretraining, LoRA, QLoRA, and DPO before selecting an original two-axis semantic comparison.

implementation.accessibility: The figure uses a linked learning question and an explicitly labelled group of two semantic sections. Objectives, data signals, effects, and update scopes are all stated in text; numbered stages, headings, and written relationships carry the full lesson without color. The established two-column primitive stacks below 640 CSS pixels with normal text wrapping and no minimum width, making it readable at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme tokens provide dark-mode contrast and shared print rules produce a high-contrast light rendering.
